dedupe_keys.name: usgs geospatial tool for mine waste volume calculations from remote sensing arcgis pro toolbox for usmin

description: An ArcGIS Pro toolbox that estimates the volume of mine waste piles. The USGS software release says it takes a polygon outline of the mine waste and elevation data from remote sensing and computes the volume with a linear regression method described in an accompanying publication, and that it was developed for the USGS USMIN Mineral Deposit Database, with inputs and operation matching the USMIN database schema. The source code is published on the USGS code repository (code.usgs.gov) as a 2025 software release, free under the CC0 1.0 public domain dedication, with the DOI registered on 24 February 2026. Coverage is any mine site with a waste outline and elevation data; it was built around United States sites in USMIN. Caveats: it needs a licensed copy of ESRI ArcGIS Pro, and the accuracy of the regression method is given in the publication, not the page read. For simulation it gives waste pile volumes to estimate the material at risk of slope failure or erosion in floods, and the mass that remediation or reprocessing for critical minerals would move. Related catalogue records include the USMIN prospect- and mine-related features and the USMIN commodity deposit data releases.
